children: The Indian rupee opened flat versus the US dollar on September 8,, caught once again between pressure from higher oil prices, dollar demand from companies looking to hedge their FX exposure and the central bank's persistent presence in the market.
The rupee opened almost flat at 94.51 per dollar, compared with Monday’s close of 94.49.

According to Finrex, rupee to open at 94.48 this morning ( if RBI allows it to open there) and stay in a range of 94.00 to 94.75 as crude oil stay near to $ 97 level while dollar index falls to 98.74 and RBI continues to sell $ keeping rupee within the range.
Oil companies will continue to buy $ for fulfilling their requirements. Market awaits for US and India CPI data as well as the FOMC on 16th September, it added.

Asian currencies were mostly higher against the US dollar in early trade, led by the South Korean won, which gained 0.40%, followed by the Japanese yen at 0.38%. The Taiwan dollar rose 0.14%, while the Philippines peso and Indonesian rupiah strengthened 0.05% and 0.01%, respectively. The Thai baht, Malaysian ringgit and Singapore dollar also edged higher, while the Chinese renminbi was marginally weaker, declining 0.01%.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies, was a touch weaker at 98.83 amid yen strength.
That left the euro and sterling both 0.06% stronger, last at $1.1628 and $1.3549, respectively.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens almost flat at 94.51 per dollar; Asian peers trade higher
